# Brave Bunnies

## 1. Introduction

**Brave Bunnies** is a Ukrainian-Spanish co-produced animated preschool series that follows the adventures of a family of rabbits traveling in their distinctive Bunny Bus . Created by Olga Cherepanova and developed by Tim Fehrenbach, the series consists of 52 episodes, each running 7 minutes in length . The show premiered in Ukraine in 2020 and internationally in 2021, distributed globally by Aardman Animations .

The series centers on two main characters, Bop and Boo, bunny siblings who embark on adventures with their parents and four younger siblings, the Bunny Babies . Through their travels across diverse environments including jungles, savannas, forests, plains, and mountains, the Brave Bunnies encounter various animal friends, promoting themes of diversity, inclusion, and friendship .

Brave Bunnies has achieved significant international success, airing in over 80 countries across Latin America, Canada, the United Kingdom, Europe, the Nordics, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia . The show has been particularly noted for its educational value in teaching young children about acceptance and understanding of differences .

## 2. Series Overview

### 2.1 Production Background

Brave Bunnies represents the first co-production between Ukraine and Spain, developed through a partnership between Ukrainian studio Glowberry and Spanish animation studio Ánima . The series was created by Olga Cherepanova, who serves as both co-founder of Glowberry and creative producer on the project . Cherepanova has stated that her goal was to create "a series that would encourage children to be curious about the world around them, and to not only respect but celebrate its diversity" .

The series development faced significant challenges following the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which disrupted production and forced many Glowberry employees to flee Kyiv for safety reasons . In response to these circumstances, WildBrain partnered with Glowberry and Ánima to ensure the continuation of the series . Under this new arrangement, WildBrain became the majority stakeholder in the Brave Bunnies intellectual property, while Glowberry and Ánima retained minority positions .

WildBrain's Vancouver animation studio co-produced Season 2 with Glowberry and Ánima, with delivery expected to begin in June 2023 . The partnership has enabled the series to maintain its international distribution while supporting the Ukrainian creative team during challenging circumstances .

### 2.2 Format and Structure

Brave Bunnies is a 2D animated preschool series designed for children aged 2-5 . The show follows a consistent format where each 7-minute episode begins with the Bunny Bus traveling to a new location . At each stop, the main characters Bop and Boo encounter different animals and create new games to help build friendships .

The series is narrated by Chetna Pandya and features a voice cast including Wilbur Conabeare as Bop, Margot Powell as Boo, Harriet Kershaw as Bunny Ma, and Jensen Adeyanju as Bunny Pa . The music for the series was composed by Sergii Kosarenko, Denis Khrenov, and Ivan Rozin .

The technical specifications of the series include a 16:9 HD aspect ratio and Dolby Digital sound mixing . The animation style features bright, colorful designs that appeal to young children while maintaining clear visual storytelling .

### 2.3 Distribution and Reception

Brave Bunnies has achieved widespread international distribution across multiple platforms and territories. Initial broadcast deals secured by Aardman included partnerships with Nick Jr (UK), Super RTL (Germany), ABC (Australia), YLE (Finland), HOP! (Israel), PlusPlus (Ukraine), Daekyo (South Korea), and Milkshake! (UK) .

The series premiered in Ukraine on PlusPlus in 2020 and in the United Kingdom on Milkshake! in 2021 . In Canada, Family Jr. has exclusive linear broadcast rights for Season 1 . Additional distribution agreements have expanded the series' reach to include platforms in Latin America, the Middle East, Asia, and other European markets .

The show has received positive critical reception, particularly for its educational content and inclusive themes. At the MIPJunior content market, Brave Bunnies was noted as one of the most-viewed projects and received positive reviews from international experts . Alison Taylor, Director of Distribution and Business Development at Aardman, commented on the series' strong reception at industry events, stating that buyers expressed enthusiasm for the show's positive messages and engaging characters .

In the United Kingdom, the series has reached an audience of 4.4 million viewers across Channel 5's Milkshake! and Nick Jr . The show has also been successful in Japan, where the Japanese dub premiered on TV Tokyo in October 2022 and achieved top 5 ratings for preschool series .

## 3. Characters and Main Themes

### 3.1 Main Characters

The Brave Bunnies family consists of several key characters who travel together in their distinctive Bunny Bus. The primary protagonists are **Bop** and **Boo**, bunny siblings who serve as the main focus of the series . Bop is described as a brave and curious older brother who often takes the lead in their adventures . Boo is characterized as a cute and joyful little rabbit girl who loves dancing, making new friends, and eating carrot cake .

The parental figures in the series are **Bunny Ma** and **Bunny Pa**. Bunny Pa serves as the driver of the Bunny Bus, taking the family on their various adventures . The couple also has four younger children known collectively as the **Bunny Babies**, who accompany the family on their travels .

Throughout the series, the Brave Bunnies encounter numerous animal friends representing different species and backgrounds. Some of the recurring characters include Franny the Fox, Barry the Bear, Bao the Panda, Garry the Tiger, Kit the Kangaroo, and Dwayne the Moose . Each character brings unique characteristics and perspectives that help teach children about diversity and acceptance .

### 3.2 Educational Themes

The central educational theme of Brave Bunnies is to teach children about the diversity of the world around them and promote acceptance of differences . The series emphasizes the importance of making friends with others regardless of their differences and finding common ground through play and cooperation .

Olga Cherepanova has explained that the series "shows real-life examples of how to find a unique approach to each person without pressure or changing anyone's uniqueness," which she describes as essential for healthy childhood development . The creator further stated that she "created Brave Bunnies to help children all over the world communicate with different friends without any fears or stereotypes, respecting the diversity of our world" .

Each episode presents situations where the Brave Bunnies must interact with animals who have different abilities, characteristics, or backgrounds. For example, in one episode, the Bunnies meet a chameleon named Kara who inspires them to explore color-changing abilities . In another, they encounter Marvin the Mole, who lives underground and is initially afraid to come above ground . These interactions demonstrate how to approach new situations with curiosity and kindness rather than fear or prejudice.

The series also promotes problem-solving skills and creative thinking as the characters must find innovative ways to play and interact with their new friends. The show's structure encourages children to ask questions and explore their world with what the series terms "bunny bravery" .

## 4. Production and Development

### 4.1 Creative Team

The creative development of Brave Bunnies was led by **Olga Cherepanova**, who serves as both the creator of the original concept and co-founder of Glowberry . Cherepanova has been instrumental in shaping the series' educational approach and ensuring its consistent messaging about diversity and inclusion .

**Tim Fehrenbach** served as the series developer and director for the first season . His work on the series has been recognized for its ability to engage young audiences while delivering educational content effectively .

The voice cast for Brave Bunnies includes several notable performers. **Wilbur Conabeare** provides the voice of Bop, while **Margot Powell** voices Boo . **Harriet Kershaw** and **Jensen Adeyanju** respectively portray Bunny Ma and Bunny Pa . The series is narrated by **Chetna Pandya**, who provides continuity and context for the episodes .

The music for Brave Bunnies was composed by a team including **Sergii Kosarenko**, **Denis Khrenov**, and **Ivan Rozin** . Their work creates an engaging soundtrack that enhances the series' playful and educational atmosphere.

### 4.2 Production Studios

Brave Bunnies was produced through a collaborative effort between three main studios. **Glowberry**, the Ukrainian animation studio co-founded by Olga Cherepanova, served as the lead creative studio and retained creative control over the series . Glowberry's work on the series has been recognized for its high quality animation and innovative storytelling techniques .

**Ánima Estudios** from Spain partnered with Glowberry as the co-production studio . The collaboration between Glowberry and Ánima represents the first co-production between Ukraine and Spain in the animation industry . Ángel Molinero, CEO of Ánima Spain, has expressed enthusiasm about the partnership, noting that the company is "very excited about the future of the project" .

**WildBrain** joined the production team as a co-producer for Season 2 following the Russian invasion of Ukraine . WildBrain's Vancouver animation studio worked alongside Glowberry and Ánima to ensure the series' continuation during challenging circumstances . Under the new partnership structure, WildBrain became the majority stakeholder in the Brave Bunnies intellectual property, with Glowberry and Ánima maintaining minority positions .

The distribution of Brave Bunnies is handled by **Aardman Animations**, the British animation company known for productions such as Wallace & Gromit . Aardman's involvement has been crucial in securing international broadcast deals and establishing the series in global markets .

### 4.3 Technical Aspects

Brave Bunnies is produced as a 2D animated series with a technical specification designed for modern broadcast and streaming platforms . The series features a 16:9 HD aspect ratio, ensuring compatibility with contemporary television and digital viewing formats .

The audio production uses Dolby Digital sound mixing, providing high-quality audio suitable for various viewing environments . This technical approach ensures that the series can be enjoyed across different platforms while maintaining consistent audio quality.

The animation style of Brave Bunnies features bright, colorful designs that are specifically designed to appeal to preschool-aged children . The visual aesthetic combines simplicity with attention to detail, making characters and environments easily recognizable and engaging for young viewers .

The series' 7-minute episode format is designed to match the attention span of its target audience while delivering complete stories with clear educational messages . This format has proven effective in maintaining viewer engagement while ensuring that the educational content is presented in a digestible manner.

## 5. International Success and Merchandising

### 5.1 Global Distribution

Brave Bunnies has achieved remarkable international success, with Season 1 airing in more than 80 countries across multiple continents . The series' global reach spans Latin America, Canada, the United Kingdom, Europe, the Nordic countries, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia .

The series has been particularly successful in securing partnerships with major international broadcasters. In addition to the initial broadcast deals mentioned earlier, Brave Bunnies has expanded its reach through agreements with WarnerMedia for distribution in 20 territories across Southeast Asia, as well as Australia and New Zealand .

The show's success in international markets has been attributed to its universal themes of friendship and acceptance, which transcend cultural boundaries . Dan Frugtniet, managing director of Big Picture Licensing, noted that the series has "been in the works for years," but due to the crisis in Ukraine following the Russian invasion, "the series and the books take on a much more powerful meaning" .

In Japan, the series achieved particular success with its Japanese dub premiering on TV Tokyo in October 2022 . The Japanese version reached the top 5 most-watched preschool series in Japan, demonstrating the show's broad international appeal .

### 5.2 Merchandising and Consumer Products

The Brave Bunnies franchise has expanded beyond television into a comprehensive consumer products program. **Spin Master** serves as the global master toy partner for the series, launching a toy line that includes figures, playsets, games, and plush toys .

Spin Master's first collection consisted of eight toys, initially available in the United Kingdom, Australia, Italy, Germany, and Spain beginning in April 2022 . The toy line was designed to expand later in the year to mirror the global distribution of the series . The company has emphasized the educational value of their products, with James Martin, senior vice president of marketing and global business unit lead for preschool at Spin Master, stating that the toys "will provide preschoolers with engaging toys that will expand their experience as they interact and explore the wonderful world and the clever and caring characters within it" .

The merchandise program has been designed with particular attention to environmental sustainability. Spin Master created specially designed packaging that can be transformed into play props, reducing waste while enhancing the play value of the products . This approach aligns with the series' educational themes of creativity and resourcefulness.

In the publishing sector, Penguin Random House's Ladybird imprint has published a series of preschool books based on the television show . The first two titles, "Brave Bunnies Spring to the Rescue" and "Brave Bunnies Make a Friend," were released to coincide with the television series' broadcast . These books continue the series' educational themes while providing additional content for young fans.

The publishing program has expanded internationally with books debuting in Italy through Planeta Libre (an imprint of De Agostini), in Australia through Five Mile Publishing, and in the United Kingdom through Ladybird . This multi-territory publishing approach demonstrates the franchise's growing international recognition and commercial potential.

## 6. Reception and Legacy

### 6.1 Critical Reception

Brave Bunnies has received positive critical reception from industry professionals and educational experts. At the MIPJunior content market, the series was noted as one of the most-viewed projects and received favorable reviews from international broadcasting executives . The show's performance at MIPJunior was particularly significant as it demonstrated strong international interest in the series before its official broadcast launch .

Alison Taylor, Director of Distribution and Business Development at Aardman, commented on the series' reception at industry events: "We were delighted to see Brave Bunnies feature in the top screening figures at MIPJunior, and to hear first-hand from buyers about what they love about the series during our meetings at Mipcom Online+" . She further noted that the discussions with international broadcasters gave the team confidence in the series' potential for global success .

Educational professionals have praised the series for its innovative approach to teaching diversity and inclusion to young children. The show's ability to address complex social concepts in a manner accessible to preschoolers has been highlighted as a particular strength . The series has been recommended as a valuable tool for parents and educators to facilitate discussions about differences and acceptance .

The series has also been recognized for its production quality and technical achievements. The animation style, voice acting, and musical composition have all received positive comments from industry observers . The show's 7-minute format has been noted as particularly effective for maintaining young viewers' attention while delivering complete educational messages .

### 6.2 Impact and Cultural Significance

Beyond its entertainment value, Brave Bunnies has gained cultural significance as a Ukrainian cultural product that has maintained international distribution despite the challenges faced by the country following the Russian invasion . The series has become a symbol of Ukrainian creativity and resilience in the face of adversity .

Olga Cherepanova has expressed the importance of the series in promoting peace and understanding: "I'm proud and happy that this project born in Ukraine will now continue to spread around the world, helping the next generation develop respect for diversity and build relationships based on co-creation and cooperation rather than on fear and violence" . She further stated that the Ukrainian team hopes for peace and will "do everything possible for a peaceful tomorrow" .

The series' themes of friendship and acceptance have taken on additional significance in the context of global challenges. Francesca Dow, managing director of Penguin Random House Children's, noted that while the Ukraine crisis provides the series with "more urgency and power," the book deal was originally signed based on "the merits of the show's characters and story" .

The Brave Bunnies franchise has also contributed to Ukraine's cultural diplomacy efforts, with the series representing Ukrainian creative talent on the international stage. The show's success has helped to highlight Ukraine's capabilities in the animation industry and its contributions to global children's entertainment .

### 6.3 Future Development

The Brave Bunnies franchise continues to expand with the production of Season 2, which is expected to maintain the series' core themes while introducing new characters and adventures . The second season will feature the Brave Bunnies continuing their road trip around the Bunny World, encountering both old friends and new characters .

In Season 2, Bop and Boo will have "big surprises in store for small viewers as they visit their 'Best Bunny Friends' at their homes, meeting their families, exploring their unique lifestyles and finding lots of new adventures" . This expanded format will allow for deeper exploration of the series' educational themes while maintaining its engaging storytelling approach.

The partnership between WildBrain, Glowberry, and Ánima has established a strong foundation for the franchise's continued development . WildBrain's 360-degree capabilities across production, distribution, and consumer products provide opportunities for the series to expand into new markets and platforms .

The Brave Bunnies brand has also demonstrated potential for expansion into other media formats, including digital content, mobile applications, and interactive experiences. The series' strong educational foundation and engaging characters provide a platform for continued growth across multiple entertainment and educational channels .

## 7. Conclusion

Brave Bunnies represents a significant achievement in international children's animation, successfully combining entertainment value with educational content that promotes diversity, inclusion, and acceptance. Created by Olga Cherepanova and developed through a groundbreaking Ukrainian-Spanish co-production, the series has achieved remarkable global success with distribution in over 80 countries .

The series' core strength lies in its ability to teach complex social concepts to preschool-aged children through engaging storytelling and memorable characters. By following the adventures of Bop, Boo, and their family as they encounter diverse animal friends, Brave Bunnies effectively demonstrates the value of friendship across differences .

The production's resilience in the face of geopolitical challenges has added another layer of significance to the series. The partnership between WildBrain, Glowberry, and Ánima has not only ensured the continuation of the series but has also created a model for international collaboration in the animation industry .

Looking forward, Brave Bunnies appears poised for continued success and expansion. With Season 2 in production and an expanding merchandise and publishing program, the franchise demonstrates strong potential for growth across multiple platforms . The series' universal themes of friendship, curiosity, and acceptance position it well for continued international success while serving as an important educational tool for young children worldwide.

The Brave Bunnies franchise stands as a testament to the power of animation to entertain, educate, and inspire, while also serving as a bridge between cultures and promoting understanding in an increasingly interconnected world.

Penguin To Publish Books From Ukrainian Children’s Series Brave Bunnies
=======================================================================

March 23, 2022

[![Image 8: Cartoon depiction of the book cover titled Brave Bunnies Spring to the Rescue featuring three cartoon animals](https://thelicensingletter.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/32322Bunnies-150x150.jpeg)](https://thelicensingletter.com/penguin-to-publish-books-from-ukrainian-childrens-series-brave-bunnies/ "Penguin To Publish Books From Ukrainian Children’s Series Brave Bunnies")

By Gary Symons

TLL Editor in Chief

The Ladybird division of Penguin Random House will publish a series of pre-school books based on the Ukrainian children’s TV Show Brave Bunnies _._

The show is a breakout hit created by Olga Charepanova at the Ukrainian studio Glowberry, and is broadcast in more than 63 countries. The deal was brokered by Big Picture Licensing, with the agreement negotiated with PRH commissioning editor Ned Hartley.

Dan Frugtniet, managing director of Big Picture Licensing, said the deal has been in the works for years, but due to the crisis in Ukraine following the Russian invasion, the series and the books take on a much more powerful meaning.

“It’s wonderful to have found a UK publishing home for ‘Brave Bunnies’ with such a global leader as Ladybird and Penguin Random House,” said Frugtniet. “Given the terrible current events in Ukraine, the creators are keen to use ’Brave Bunnies’ to spread the important messages of friendship, diversity and inclusion which are the core DNA of the show.”

> [Beijing Lashes Out at Western Fashion Brands](https://thelicensingletter.com/beijing-strikes-out-at-western-fashion-brands/)

While the Ukraine crisis provides the series and books with more urgency and power, Penguin Random House Children’s managing director Francesca Dow also says the book deal was signed based on the merits of the show’s characters and story.

“This partnership is exciting for Ladybird because it is the result of several years of collaboration with the exceptionally skilled and creative team at Glowberry,” Dow explained. “We were first drawn to ’Brave Bunnies’ for its playful and warm ways of talking about friendship with a very young audience and are excited that our books are now available for young readers to explore.”

The Ladybird imprint is launching the first two titles in the series this month under the _Brave Bunnies Spring to the Rescue_ and _Brave Bunnies Make a Friend**.**_

Brave Bunnies follows the adventures of Bop and Boo, who live with their family on the Bunny Bus and love to explore the world. At each stop, Bop and Boo make new friends, play new games and discover a little more about the world and the people around them, spreading messages of inclusivity, friendship and respect. The first two titles with Ladybird will see Bop and Boo learning lessons about bravery, responsibility and compassion, themes that resonate for anyone living in Ukraine today.

The Brave Bunnies series launched in the UK on Channel 5’s “Milkshake!” and on Nick Jr in February and September 2021 respectively. To date, it has already reached a UK audience of 4.4 million, the broadcasters say.

6.title: WILDBRAIN ANNOUNCES WAVE OF NEW DISTRIBUTION DEALS FOR SEASONS 1 AND 2 OF ANIMATED SERIES BRAVE BUNNIES
6.content:
**New international partnerships include Milkshake! (UK), Rai Yoyo (Italy) and TeleTOON+ (Canal+ Poland)**

Toronto, ON – November 30, 2023 – WildBrain has secured a wave of international distribution deals for the beloved animated preschool series, _Brave Bunnies._ The news comes as producers WildBrain, Glowberry, Anima Kitchent and KidsMe launch a brand-new second season of the highly popular series, following last year’s announcement of their global partnership on the brand.

Under the partnership, WildBrain handles global distribution of the series, while Glowberry manages distribution in Ukraine, KidsMe in Italy, and Anima Kitchent in Spain. In consumer products, WildBrain’s leading agency, WildBrain CPLG, handles licensing and merchandising worldwide, outside of Ukraine, where licensing is handled by Glowberry, and Italy, where licensing and merchandising is handled by KidsMe.

![Image 1: Two animated blue bunnies and a teal rhino look right to the viewer and hold up colourful animal toys.](https://static.wixstatic.com/media/449abe_bc331138eb8c4cecab947e79cd278c6e~mv2.png/v1/fill/w_740,h_416,al_c,q_85,usm_0.66_1.00_0.01,enc_avif,quality_auto/449abe_bc331138eb8c4cecab947e79cd278c6e~mv2.png)

The show’s curious and adventurous sibling bunnies, Boo and Bop, continue their global adventure through new distribution partnerships inked with TeleTOON+ (Canal+ Poland), Channel 5’s preschool strand, Milkshake! (UK), and Rai Yoyo (Italy) for both season one and two. Additionally, season one has been newly picked up by CNC Media International (South Korea) and Stan (Australia). Season one is also now available on the WildBrain+ SVOD channel on Comcast in the US. These international deals reflect the global appeal of the brand, adding to the list of platforms in more than 80 countries across LatAm, Canada, the UK, Europe, Nordics, the Middle East, Asia and Australia that have previously picked up the series. YouTube also remains a popular destination for _Brave Bunnies_ fans, where the preschool brand continues to develop a global audience with new uploads each week on the official [Brave Bunnies YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCTtRc8rZrf6753hXFTvl-PQ).

Caroline Tyre, VP Global Sales and Rights Strategy at WildBrain, said: “It’s easy to understand why we continue to see strong demand for _Brave Bunnies_ from broadcasters and streamers worldwide. Through catchy songs, adorable characters and big adventures, the charming series engages kids everywhere, appealing to their sense of joy and imagination. It also fosters values of curiosity, creativity, acceptance and openness, encouraging kids to discover what they might have in common with new friends, while also celebrating what makes them different.”

Olga Cherepanova, Glowberry co-founder and Creative Producer on the series, said: “With _Brave Bunnies_, I wanted to create a series that would encourage children to be curious about the world around them, and to not only respect but celebrate its diversity. It’s rewarding to see children around the world connect so strongly with these important values through the show’s lovable characters and their adventures.”

Aimed at kids aged 2–5, _Brave Bunnies_(104 x 7’ total) follows Boo and her big brother, Bop, as they travel the world with their Ma and Pa in their Bunny Bus. Season two, which was produced by WildBrain’s Vancouver animation studio and Anima Kitchent’s studio in the Canary Islands, sees the Brave Bunnies continue their road trip adventure around the Bunny World, encountering old friends and making more new ones. Boo and Bop have some big surprises in store for small viewers as they visit their “Best Bunny Friends” at their homes, meeting their families, exploring their unique lifestyles and sharing new adventures.

**For more information, please contact:**

**About WildBrain**

At WildBrain we inspire imaginations through the wonder of storytelling. As a leader in 360° IP management, we are experts in content creation, audience engagement and global licensing, cultivating and growing love for our own and partner brands with kids and families around the world. With approximately 13,000 half-hours of filmed entertainment in our library—one of the world’s most extensive—we are home to such treasured franchises as Peanuts, Teletubbies, Strawberry Shortcake, Yo Gabba Gabba!, Caillou, Inspector Gadget and Degrassi. WildBrain’s mission is to create exceptional entertainment experiences that captivate and delight fans both young and young at heart.

Our studios produce such award-winning series as _The Snoopy Show_; _Snoopy in Space_; _Strawberry Shortcake: Berry in the Big City; Sonic Prime_; _Chip and Potato_; _Teletubbies Let's Go!_ and many more. Enjoyed in more than 150 countries on over 500 platforms, our content is everywhere kids and families view entertainment, including YouTube, where our network has garnered over 1 trillion minutes of watch time. Our television group owns and operates some of Canada’s most-viewed family entertainment channels. WildBrain CPLG, our leading consumer-products and location-based entertainment agency, represents our owned and partner properties in every major territory worldwide.

WildBrain is headquartered in Canada with offices worldwide and trades on the Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: WILD). Visit us at [wildbrain.com](https://www.wildbrain.com/).

**About Glowberry**

Glowberry is a dynamic Ukrainian creative production company that develops high-quality 360° content for kids and families worldwide, founded in 2009 as a publishing house. Glowberry, now a strategic partner of FILM.UA Group, grew into a production company that works with the best Ukrainian and international professionals to create animated children's content. Company partners are global leaders in animation, broadcasting, film production and licensing. Today, one of the key projects for our team is the _Brave Bunnie_ s animated series.

“We believe that creativity, openness to the diversity of the world, and the ability to enjoy life make children's lives exciting, and we are guided by this in our work. We are extremely proud of the team of professional artists and professionals from various fields that we have managed to assemble to work on Glowberry products” – says Olga Cherepanova, Glowberry co-founder and Creative Producer. The projects of the Glowberry professional team are highly acclaimed by international experts and became shortlist finalists of global animation festivals like Cartoon Forum, Animation Production Days, Cartoon 360, Annecy International Animated Film Festival (MIFA), Ottawa International Animation Festival and The Financing Forum for Kids Content.

**About Anima Kitchent**

Anima Kitchent is an animation company with more than 10 years in the animation sector. A team with extensive expertise focusing on creating, producing, distributing, and marketing entertainment brands for children and young audiences. They also offer their services to third-party entities.

Anima Kitchent specializes in creating IPs that can adapt to various platforms including TV, YouTube, apps, web and video games.

Anima Kitchent's most significant project is Cleo&Cuquin - Familia Telerín. This project is accompanied by other productions such as Lea&Pop, Titto Lizzardo, PINY Institute of New York, among others. Anima's content has a strong presence on digital platforms, (Netflix, Cartoonito, Spotify) managing more than 148 YouTube channels with over 43 million subscribers.

**About KidsMe**

KidsMe is specialized in the development, production, content curation and distribution of local and European content dedicated to the Kids&Family target. The Children Content Factory part of De Agostini Editore was born in 2020.

From 2009 to 2020, the Team that is now part of KidsMe has produced and co-produced more than 1,500 hours of content for the target meant for the Group's channels. Today, after a decade of experience, the company has expanded and strengthened its core business focusing on the production and distribution of Live Action and Animation Entertainment content for the Kids&Family target.

Its production focuses on all television genres intended for the target, such as Live Action, Animation, Preschool, Educational, Factual Entertainment and Game Show. KidsMe has produced, co-produced and licensed many products for pay and free-to-air TV channels, such as DeAKids, DeAJunior, Super!, Boing, Rai YoYo, RaiGulp, as well as various contents for OTT platforms like discovery+.

Brave Bunnies glows at MIPJunior
================================

Brave Bunnies – a 52 x 7 minute 2D pre-school series created by Olga Cherepanova, currently in production with family entertainment company Anima and distributed globally by Aardman, has received positive reviews from the most influential international experts and became one of the projects receiving most viewed programmes in the [MIPJunior](https://www.mipjunior.com/en-gb.html) screenings library.

The animated series, which is yet to see its international premiere on the world’s TV channels, received a very positive response when presented at entertainment content market MIPCOM earlier this month, and was charted as the second most watched project during the first week of the market.

**Alison Taylor, Director of Distribution and Business Development at Aardman says**: “We were delighted to see Brave Bunnies feature in the top screening figures at MIPJunior, and to hear first-hand from buyers about what they love about the series during our meetings at Mipcom Online+. From the discussions had at the market, we’re confident that we will soon be in a position to announce further partnerships on the brand, in addition to the excellent broadcaster partners already announced.”

**Olga Cherepanova, Author of the original idea of the series and Creative Producer at Glowberry added**: “We are incredibly happy that Brave Bunnies have managed to attract so much attention from the MIPJunior participants, since their expertise is of great importance to us and proves that we are moving in the right direction and are indeed creating the content of international level. As for now, we have quite an ambitious plan, which is gradually being implemented – to captivate the hearts of an audience of at least fifty, and better even a hundred countries of the world.“

**Ángel Molinero, CEO (Spain) at Ánima concluded**: “Brave Bunnies is such a great show, the amazing performance it had during MipJunior proves it. We are honoured to be part of such a unique show and eager to introduce the Bunny family to kids all around the world.”

Deals for the series have been secured with Nick Jr (UK), Super RTL (Germany), ABC (Australia), YLE (Finland), HOP! (Israel), PlusPlus (Ukraine), Daekyo (South Korea) and Milkshake! (UK).

Brave Bunnies follows a family of courageous and curious Bunnies as they seek adventure and exploration, travelling on the Bunny Bus. Every episode in the series, directed by Tim Fehrenbach starts with a Bunny Bus-ride. On each stop, brother and sister Bunnies, Bop and Boo discover different animals, creating new games to help build new friendships. The series shows children the diversity of the world, encouraging viewers to accept differences, no matter how big or small.

[Brave Bunnies](https://bravebunnies.com/) is due to launch in winter 2020.

================================================================

New Wildbrain, Glowberry and Ánimas’ agreement ensures the continued production of the popular preschool animated series despite its disruption caused by the Russian invasion of Ukraine.

By [Debbie Diamond Sarto](https://awn.com/users/debbie-diamond-sarto "View Debbie Diamond Sarto's profile.") | Monday, December 5, 2022 at 10:13am

In [2D](https://awn.com/2d), [Business](https://awn.com/business), [CG](https://awn.com/cg), [Licensing](https://awn.com/licensing), [People](https://awn.com/people), [Television](https://awn.com/television) | [ANIMATIONWorld](https://awn.com/animationworld), [Headline News](https://awn.com/news) | Geographic Region: [All](https://awn.com/regions/all)

[![Image 6: Two blue rabbits skipping rope outside, with a grey mosquito flying above them](https://awn.com/sites/default/files/styles/inline/public/image/featured/bbf_kangaroo_and_bunnies-1280.jpg?itok=zAstanlc)](https://www.awn.com/sites/default/files/styles/original/public/image/featured/bbf_kangaroo_and_bunnies-1280.jpg?itok=KrovKEoH)

WildBrain has partnered with Ukrainian-based Glowberry to bring the _Brave Bunnies_ preschool brand into its kids’ and family franchise portfolio. Under the arrangement, WildBrain has assured the continuation of the popular series disrupted by the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Working with Glowberry and the Ibero-American animation studio, Ánima, WildBrain will lead global management of the franchise, leveraging its 360° capabilities across production, distribution, and consumer products. Glowberry co-founder Olga Cherepanova created _Brave Bunnies_ and is the series’ creative director.

_Brave Bunnies_ Season 2 will be co-produced by WIldbrain’s Vancouver studio, with delivery expected in June 2023. WildBrain CPLG, the company’s dedicated consumer products agency, will manage licensing and merchandising worldwide. In addition, the company’s own Family Jr. channel has picked up _Brave Bunnies_ Season 1 (produced by Glowberry and Ánima) for exclusive linear telecast in Canada. Glowberry retains distribution and licensing rights for the brand in Ukraine, while Ánima has distribution rights in Spain. The three-way partnership, which Big Picture Licensing facilitated, sees WildBrain become the majority stakeholder in the _Brave Bunnies_ IP, with Glowberry and Ánima as minority stakeholders.

“_Brave Bunnies_ is a kids’ property born of tremendous creative vision and has the potential to be a major preschool franchise, having already established a solid foundation with audiences through compelling content and consumer products,” commented Wildbrain CEO Eric Ellenbogen. “Following the terrible events in Ukraine this year, we saw it as vital to ensure the future of this wonderful property, and we couldn’t be more pleased now to be collaborating with Olga Cherepanova and her Glowberry team, along with the creative team at Ánima, on the next big adventures for the _Brave Bunnies_.”

The 2D-animated series for kids ages 2-5 follows the adventures of two curious and inspiring bunny siblings—Boo and Bop—who create joy and excitement in their lives by bravely seeking out new friends, games, and experiences. The series fosters curiosity, creativity, eagerness, openness, and responsibility while encouraging kids to ask, “What if...?”

[![Image 7: A moose and two blue creatures with a carrots and green hearts on their heads ride in a sled through the winter landscape](https://www.awn.com/sites/default/files/styles/inline/public/image/attached/1058727-bbfmooseandbunnies-1280.jpg?itok=KSct9Iqx)](https://www.awn.com/sites/default/files/styles/original/public/image/attached/1058727-bbfmooseandbunnies-1280.jpg?itok=o88KehpQ)

“I created _Brave Bunnies_ to help children all over the world communicate with different friends without any fears or stereotypes, respecting the diversity of our world,” shared Cherepanova. “Each episode of _Brave Bunnies_ shows real-life examples of how to find a unique approach to each person without pressure or changing anyone’s uniqueness. This idea is essential for healthy childhood development.”

Adding, “Unfortunately, after the Russian invasion of Ukraine, the Glowberry team faced significant challenges. Many employees were forced to flee Kyiv because of personal safety and the lives of their loved ones. But thanks to the support of partners like WildBrain and Ánima, now we have the opportunity to continue to create and share _Brave Bunnies_ together.”

“I’m proud and happy that this project born in Ukraine will now continue to spread around the world, helping the next generation develop respect for diversity and build relationships based on co-creation and cooperation rather than on fear and violence,” concluded Cherepanova. “On behalf of the Ukrainian team, I want to express my deep gratitude to all the partners and talented people working together on Brave Bunnies, who have done so much despite the challenges we all faced. We do hope for peace in Ukraine and will do everything possible for a peaceful tomorrow.”

“From Ánima, we want to thank both WildBrain and Glowberry,” said Ánima, Spain CEO Ángel Molinero. “We are very excited about the future of the project, and we believe WildBrain is the perfect partner to give continuity to the Brave Bunnies brand.”

_Brave Bunnies_ Season 1 is on kids' platforms in more than 80 countries across LatAm, Canada, the UK, Europe, Nordics, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia. A complimentary toy line for _Brave Bunnies_ was launched by kids’ entertainment company Spin Master in Germany and Italy earlier this year. In addition, the franchise’s first books have debuted in Italy from publisher Planeta Libre, an imprint of De Agostini, who are also co-producers of the animated series; in Australia from Five Mile Publishing; and in the UK from Ladybird, an imprint of Penguin Random House.

In season one of _Brave Bunnies_ (52 x 7’), Boo and Bop are on a big adventure in the Bunny Bus with Ma and Pa and their four wee siblings, the Bunny Babies. Together, they bravely explore the Bunny World, traveling to the jungle, savannah, forest, plains, and mountains. Along the way, Boo and Bop meet new animal children, including a tiger, kangaroo, bear, fox, and llama. Despite their differences, they always find a way to make friends and play new games!

For season two (52 x 7’), the _Brave Bunnies_ continue their road trip adventure around the Bunny World, encountering a few old friends and making more new ones! In this season, Boo and Bop have some big surprises in store for small viewers as they visit their “Best Bunny Friends” at their homes, meet their families, explore their unique lifestyles, and find new adventures.

_Source: WIldbrain_

Story
-----

This cute animated series follows a bunny family as they travel on the Bunny Bus. These curious and brave little bunnies have all sorts of adventures and explorations. At every stop, the bunnies meet different animals who quickly become friends through the games they play together. This series emphasizes diversity, friendship and acceptance.

### Who are the main characters of Brave Bunnies?

**Bop:** He's a clever and friendly little rabbit boy. He's never bored and always looking for new people to meet and things to do. 

**Boo:** She's Bop's sister and she's a cute and joyful little rabbit girl. She loves dancing and making new friends and eating carrot cake. 

**Pa:** He drives his family around in the Bunny Bus, looking for new adventures. He's fun-loving and inventive. 

**Ma:** She's very caring and loves outdoor activities. She plays the ukelele. 

**Bunny Babies:** Bop and Boo's baby siblings, four little rabbits, three boys and one girl. 

**Bao:** A Chinese panda, and one of the friends the Bunny family meet on their journey. 

**Bev:** A little beaver girl who shows Bop and Boo how to build things. 

**Carmen:** She's a very elegant flamingo, who loves to dance. 

**Dwayne:** He's a moose who's very good at skiing. Bop and Boo want to try it out.

### Production studio: Glowberry

The information provided on this page about Brave Bunnies isn’t endorsed by the creators or the production. It has been compiled by fans of the character(s) who want to share their passion. Feel free to share it if you also love this cartoon!

### ​**​动画介绍​**​

《勇敢兔家族》是由​**​乌克兰Glowberry工作室​**​原创的启蒙冒险动画，于2019年首播，已登陆全球80余国儿童频道。故事围绕兔子兄妹​**​波波（Bop）​**​与​**​小布（Boo）​**​展开，他们与父母及四个兔宝宝弟妹共同驾驶一辆​**​天蓝色兔兔巴士​**​，穿越森林、草原、沙漠、雪原等多元生态区。每段旅程均以“探索未知地域+结识新朋友”为核心，通过7分钟单元剧形式，构建微型社会学实验场——当兔兄妹用好奇心和包容力化解与狐狸、老虎等“天敌”的隔阂时，动画传递出​**​“差异非壁垒，而是对话起点”​**​的普世价值观。

创作背景充满人文温度：2022年基辅战火蔓延时，团队在地铁站修改脚本、防空洞录制配乐、跨国协作传输分镜稿，使作品成为“战火中播种希望”的象征。视觉上采用​**​双轨色彩编码​**​：自然场景以饱和度极高的水彩质感渲染花瓣露珠，角色设计则融合​**​布偶剧场元素​**​——兔耳用毛绒纹理勾边，猛虎斑纹转化为暖橙色波浪线，弱化生物链的残酷性，构建童话版地球村。

* * *

### ​**​IMDB评分​**​

*   ​**​综合评分​**​：​**​暂无权威评分​**​（学龄前动画未录入IMDB体系）
*   ​**​口碑聚焦​**​： “当兔兄妹教小狼用胡萝卜代替骨头玩抛接游戏时，偏见消融在孩子的笑声里” —— _Preschool Education Journal_

争议点：部分动物保护组织质疑“老虎与兔子野餐”脱离自然法则，制作方回应称“以童话逻辑解构现实隔阂”。

### ​**​动画亮点​**​

#### ​**​1. 跨物种社交启蒙系统​**​

*   ​**​冲突转化设计​**​：

在《与狼共舞》单元中，小狼伍夫（Woof）初时拒绝参与兔兄妹的抛球游戏，执着于独玩火箭玩具。波波提出“What if…我们将火箭绑上胡萝卜？”的开放式诘问，最终三方共创“胡萝卜火箭接力赛”，将排斥转化为协作创新。
*   ​**​文化符号植入​**​：

墨西哥亡灵节特辑中，拉丁裔小兔薇妲（Vida）带领团队用万寿菊铺成彩虹路，糖骷髅化作友谊勋章，在欢愉中传递“死亡亦可温馨纪念”的生命观。

#### ​**​2. 家庭关系动态建模​**​

*   ​**​育儿范式革新​**​：

兔父母拒绝“指令式教育”：当波波因失败沮丧时，父亲递上自制“情绪汤”（混合莓果与薄荷），母亲则展开“友谊地图”引导回忆快乐时刻，展现​**​情感支持优于结果评判​**​的现代教育观。

#### ​**​3. 生态教育游戏化​**​

*   ​**​自然互动机关​**​：

兔兔巴士实为移动实验室：点击车窗触发AR生态系统投影（如扫描沙漠生成地下水脉图），儿童观众可通过官方APP同步收集“友谊勋章”激活隐藏动画。

    *   ​**​2-3岁​**​：侧重感官互动（《雪地派对》中踩脚印琴键造旋律）；

#### ​**​代表性故事母题​**​

*   ​**​差异重构论​**​：

在《虎王的皇冠》中，老虎加里（Garry）因惧怕弄脏王冠拒绝玩泥巴，兔兄妹将泥潭重塑为“陶艺工坊”，使王冠进阶为镶泥釉勋章——​**​“高贵源于接纳不完美”​**​的价值重构；
*   ​**​记忆物质化​**​：

兔妈妈的“故事围巾”随旅途延长而增织新纹样（熊猫竹林绣纹、沙漠星轨图等），将抽象经历转化为可触摸的成长图腾。

* * *

### ​**​观众反馈与影响​**​

#### ​**​教育实践革新​**​

*   ​**​课堂革命​**​：

波士顿幼儿园开发“Brave Bunnies社交卡”，儿童抽取角色卡破解冲突情境（如抽到“狐狸卡”需设计共享游戏），全球50+教育机构引入该教案；
*   ​**​特殊群体关怀​**​：

听障儿童通过手语版理解“声音振动”单元（小布用手语节奏替代歌唱），乌克兰难民儿童绘制“友谊地图”传递战火中的希望。

#### ​**​文化共鸣现象​**​

*   ​**​战火中的创作信仰​**​：

2022年基辅围城期间，粉丝发起#CarrotForPeace活动，全球儿童邮寄胡萝卜画作至工作室，印度孩子附言：“帮兔兔找新朋友”；
*   ​**​衍生公益行动​**​：

乐高推出“兔兔巴士”套装（编号76901），部分收益捐赠战区儿童心理重建项目。

### ​**​动画总结​**​

《勇敢兔家族》在三个维度重塑了儿童社交启蒙的范式：

1.   ​**​差异的光合作用​**​

当狐狸弗朗妮（Franny）的尖爪撕破彩球，而波波用树胶将其修补为“彩虹万花筒”时，​**​生物链的对抗性被创造性协作解构​**​——动画宣告：所谓“天敌”，不过是尚未翻译的友谊方言。兔兔巴士碾过的不只是地理疆界，更是认知的藩篱。
2.   ​**​传统的非暴力革命

虎王加里的皇冠从权力图腾蜕变为陶艺勋章，小狼伍夫的火箭玩具从独占品进化为共享载具​**​。动画以温柔姿态颠覆符号霸权：当孩子们目睹猛兽为友谊收敛爪牙时，“强者”的定义被重写为“守护差异的勇气”。
3.   记忆的织物哲学

兔妈妈腰间的故事围巾，实为​**​集体记忆的可视化史诗​**​——每道新增的纹样都是跨文化对话的结绳记事。这条无限延展的织物，将敦煌飞天的飘带、玛雅太阳纹与北欧极光经纬交织，证明人类文明本属同一匹锦缎。

> 正如战火中坚持创作的动画师Olga所言：“我们缝补弹孔的方式，是教孩子用好奇心穿透偏见。当兔兔巴士的车灯刺破基辅夜雾时，光锥所及处皆是希望。”

Spin Master Named Master Toy Partner for Glowberry’s ‘Brave Bunnies’
====================================================================

November 22, 2021 by [James Zahn](https://toybook.com/author/jzahn/ "Go to: ")

![Image 8: Toy Partner promotional poster with Brave Bunnies artwork of blue rabbit characters with toys](https://toybook.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2021/11/SpinMaster_Glowberry.jpg)

Source: Spin Master

[Spin Master](https://toybook.com/tag/spin-master) inked a deal with Glowberry to serve as the global master toy [licensee](https://toybook.com/tag/licensing) for the Ukrainian studio’s _Brave Bunnies_.

The animated preschool series from Glowberry and Spanish animation studio Anima follows the Brave Bunnies family as they explore the world around them with a focus on socialization and being inclusive and accepting of others around them.

Under the new deal, Spin Master will launch a Brave Bunnies toy line next year that includes figures, playsets, games, and plush.

“_Brave Bunnies_ is filled with opportunities for play and Spin Master’s collection will provide preschoolers with engaging toys that will expand their experience as they interact and explore the wonderful world and the clever and caring characters within it,” says James Martin, senior vice president of marketing and global business unit lead, preschool at Spin Master.

#### Related: [Spin Master Posts Record-Breaking Q3 Earnings While Navigating Supply Chain Issues](https://toybook.com/spin-master-posts-record-breaking-q3-earnings-while-navigating-supply-chain-issues/ "Go to: Spin Master Posts Record-Breaking Q3 Earnings While Navigating Supply Chain Issues")

Spin Master says that its first collection of eight toys will be available in the UK, Australia, Italy, Germany, and Spain beginning in April. The line will expand later in the year to mirror the global distribution of the series. As of this month, Brave Bunnies airs in a dozen countries with more coming soon.

13.content:
[![Image 1: Licensing.biz logo, with the word licensing in bold white font and .biz in bold blue font against a black background](https://licensing.biz/wp-content/themes/FortemTheme/images/licensinglogo.png)](https://licensing.biz/)

[![Image 2: Paw Patrol Rescue Wheels Championship is available for PlayStation 5, PlayStation 4, and Nintendo Switch](https://licensing.biz/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/2_PP-RWC_TOY-WORLD_L-SKY-1_677X226_v1-1.jpg)](https://outrightgames.com/games/paw-patrol-rescue-wheels-championship/?utm_source=display&utm_medium=ads&utm_campaign=PAW+Patrol+Rescue+Wheels&utm_id=toyworldmagazine&utm_term=PAW+Patrol)

[![Image 3: PAW Patrol Rescue Wheels Championship game available for multiple consoles](https://licensing.biz/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/2_PP-RWC_TOY-WORLD_L-SKY-CONVERSION_632x226_v2.jpg)](https://outrightgames.com/games/paw-patrol-rescue-wheels-championship/?utm_source=display&utm_medium=ads&utm_campaign=PAW+Patrol+Rescue+Wheels&utm_id=toyworldmagazine&utm_term=PAW+Patrol)

**Glowberry, the Ukrainian creator of popular kids’ series _Brave Bunnies_, has announced a licensing agreement with WarnerMedia to broadcast the series in 20 territories across Southeast Asia, as well as Australia and New Zealand.**

The deal was secured for Glowberry by its exclusive content distribution partner, Aardman, who have been leading the charge for _Brave Bunnies_ with tier-one broadcasters around the world.

The series will premiere on the Cartoonito pre-school programming block available daily on Cartoon Network, which launched on March 28 in Southeast Asia, and will debut in Australia and New Zealand in July.

The series will also be available to stream in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Hong Kong on HBO GO. This latest deal strengthens the relationship with WarnerMedia as _Brave Bunnies_ was also acquired by HBO Max for LATAM. The series will premiere mid-2022.

Olga Cherepanova, author and creative producer of _Brave Bunnies_, says: “We are delighted that a show we have been working on so passionately has been expanding so fast. I’m happy that alongside WarnerMedia we will reach a new audience in APAC. Our partner Aardman continues to do a great job signing up the best broadcast partners for our bunnies.”

Robin Gladman, Head of Acquisitions at Aardman, comments: “It’s a great pleasure to be working with our friends at Glowberry, to help bring Brave Bunnies to the world. The team from Ukraine are constantly in our thoughts in their current plight. Friendship and diversity sit at the core of this fabulous show, these messages are more important now than ever, and we are thrilled Warner have decided to come on board across so many territories.”

**Ladybird is launching a series of pre-school titles with _Brave Bunnies_, the global Ukrainian children’s brand. Ladybird Commissioning Editor Ned Hartley acquired UK publishing rights to the brand from [Big Picture Licensing](https://www.bigpicturelicensing.com/), who are the master-agent for Brave Bunnies across EMEA & APAC regions.**

Dan Frugtniet, MD of Big Picture Licensing, says: “It’s wonderful to have found a UK publishing home for Brave Bunnies with such a global leader as Ladybird & Penguin Random House. Given the terrible current events in Ukraine, the creators are keen to use Brave Bunnies to spread the important messages of friendship, diversity and inclusion which are the core DNA of the show.”

_Brave Bunnies_ follows the adventures of bunnies Bop and Boo, who live with their family on the Bunny Bus and love to explore the world. At each stop, Bop and Boo make new friends, play new games and discovering a little more about the world and people around them, spreading messages of inclusivity, friendship and respect.

Created by Olga Cherepanova at Glowberry, _Brave Bunnies_ is broadcast in over 63 countries. It launched in the UK on Milkshake! (on Channel 5) and Nick Jr. in February and September 2021 respectively. To date it has reached a UK audience of 4.4million. _Brave Bunnies_ ranked as the #1 commercial channel in its slots for its premiere.

Ladybird launches the first two titles in the series in March 2022: _Brave Bunnies Spring to the Rescue_ and _Brave Bunnies Make a Friend_, which see Bop and Boo learning lessons about bravery, responsibility and compassion.

Francesca Dow, MD of Penguin Random House Children’s, says: “This partnership is exciting for Ladybird because it is the result of several years of collaboration with the exceptionally skilled and creative team at Glowberry. We were first drawn to Brave Bunnies for its playful and warm ways of talking about friendship with a very young audience, and are excited that our books are now available for young readers to explore, bringing the internationally successful Brave Bunnies to existing and new fans in the UK.”

Glowberry, creator of the popular preschool animation series BRAVE BUNNIES, and Big Picture Licensing (BPL), its exclusive licensing agent for UK & Eire and master-agent across EMEA and APAC, plus Centa IP, the licensing agent for ANZ region, have signed agreements with four new partners for a range of products that will expand the offerings for the hit kids’ brand.

New deals for the BRAVE BUNNIES brand include Caprice Australia, PMI, Five Mile Press (the publishing division of Regency Media) and Roy Lowe & Sons.

In Australia and New Zealand, Caprice is on-board for apparel, footwear, bags, and home décor. The deal with Five Mile Press includes sticker books, activity books, colouring books, novelty books, flap books and educational books.

The PMI deal spans a wide range of products, including Homeware, BTS/Stationary and Collectables to launch worldwide. Roy Lowe & Sons have signed on for the UK in their specialist category.

Dan Frugtniet, MD at Big Picture Licensing, says:“Big Picture Licensing is very proud to have been working with BRAVE BUNNIES for the last two years… to appoint key strategic partners, licensing agents and new licensees around the world for this beautiful preschool property.

“Our first-wave licensees include Spin Master, Penguin Random House and DeAgostini/Planeta Libra; they are all aligned and launching their products in 2021-22, and now PMI, Roy Lowe & Sons, Five Mile Press and Caprice are all aboard the Bunny Bus for launch in 2022 across Global, UK and Australia/NZ respectively. We are thrilled to welcome to them to the BRAVE BUNNIES family!”

BRAVE BUNNIES, created by Glowberry in coproduction with the leading animation studio Anima, tells the story of the curious and courageous Brave Bunnies Family. They go on a BIG Journey to explore the diverse world around them and find new friends. A unique aspect of the show is its focus on helping children with their first socialization through various games. It also teaches kids to accept the differences of others and be courageous in exploring the world around them.

[Glowberry](https://glowberry.com/), creator of the popular kids’ series BRAVE BUNNIES, and [Big Picture Licensing](https://www.bigpicturelicensing.com/) (BPL), its exclusive licensing agent, have announced the signing of Penguin Random House as a strategic multi-territory licensee, joining DeA Planeta Libri as publishing partners.

A publishing team and series creators are already at work on the first series of books about the journey and adventures of the Brave Bunnies and their friends.

The first products to hit the shelves will be picture books, board books and little libraries, which will launch Easter 2022 around the world.

The deal was made with Ned Hartley, Commissioning Editor, Ladybird, who says:“We fell in love with BRAVE BUNNIES as soon as we saw it, and we knew that it would work brilliantly as publishing. We’re sure that these books are going to hop off the shelves!”

The contract with Ladybird, Penguin Random House Children’s UK is a crucial stage in the sequence of successful deals for the Ukrainian team, following contracts with Spin Master Toys Company, DeAgostini Publisher, and other internationally acclaimed companies.

Olga Cherepanova, the author of the idea behind the BRAVE BUNNIES series and Glowberry’s creative producer, has also announced several regional and European licensing deals that are now are in their final stages.

The series already airs in 63 countries, including the UK, Italy, Spain, Norway, Germany, Sweden, Israel, Latvia, South Korea, Finland, Australia, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Ukraine.

Italian publisher DeA Planeta Libri, a subsidiary of Grupo Planeta and DeAgostini, has become the first company in the Italian market to publish books based on the popular kids’ series _Brave Bunnies,_ produced by Ukrainian production team Glowberry. The deal was arranged by KidsMe, the distributor and agent for Brave Bunnies in Italy.

The book collection includes sticker books Amici Incredibili (Incredible Friends) and In Giro per il Mondo (Around the World), as well as hardcover books Eroi Controvento (Brave Heroes), Strisce da Esploratore (Hidden Treasure), and Pulizia Cosmica (A Great Mess).

In October, DeA Planeta Libri launched the books in leading book chains across 800 stores nationwide, as well as on online platforms. Besides dedicated book stores, the books are available in over 300 mass-market outlets across Italy.

Olga Cherepanova, originator of the _Brave Bunnies_ concept and Creative Producer of the series, says: “The first release of books based on _Brave Bunnies_ is a major event for the series team. It’s another step toward building a fully fledged universe around the _Brave Bunnies_ series and its characters. Each new viewer of the series is motivating and inspiring us to go forward. That’s why we are always excited to gain new fans and connect with the established fanbase in a new way — through print media.

“We are proud to work with the talented team of KidsMe and DeA Planeta Libri, the undisputed market leader.”

KidsMe became Glowberry’s first partner and paved the way for the worldwide distribution of the project, which has included a global toy contract with toy company Spin Master, a deal with publisher Penguin Random House, and more.

Brenda Maffuchi, Chief of Co-Productions, Licensing and Sales Officer at KidsMe says: “We are very happy to have confirmed this first license for Brave Bunnies in Italy. It will be the first of many licenses and contracts we are working on in the Italian market. We are hoping to confirm these agreements very soon because we know that Brave Bunnies is an IP with great potential and we can’t wait to see the brand’s products in the Italian market.”

In Italy, BRAVE BUNNIES premiered this spring on RAIYoYo. The series first aired on the streaming service Rai Play and began airing on Rai YoYo nationwide on April 19.

Aimed at preschool kids and based on an original idea by Olga Cherepanova, Brave Bunnies is co-created with Spanish animation studio Ánima and is distributed internationally by Aardman Animations.

Big Picture Licensing has been appointed the exclusive licensing agent for the UK and Eire, and master agent across EMEA and APAC for the animated pre-school series Brave Bunnies.

Created and developed by the Ukrainian creative production hub, Glowberry, the new series aims to blend the traditional feel of a pre-school property with modern and relevant themes of diversity and inclusivity. It follows the adventures of two brave and curious bunnies who journey through their world on the Bunny Bus in search of new friends.

52 episodes make up season one that, thanks to a partnership with Aardman as global content distributor, has already been placed with the likes of Milkshake and Nick Jr in the UK, SuperRTL in Germany, ABC in Australia, SVT in Sweden and more. The show has already gone live in some territories, with further international roll-out scheduled during Q1 2021.

On a global scale, Brave Bunnies has appointed a portfolio of licensing agents that includes DeAgnostini in Italy, and LaPanaderia, the master agent for the property in Latin America. Meanwhile, Big Picture Licensing has signed up a roster of leading agents in their respective regions, including CPLG for Benelux, Nordics, CEE, and Southern Europe, CLM for Africa, Centa IP in Australia and New Zealand, and Mediogen in Israel.

Brave Bunnies licensed products are set to roll out from Easter 2022, with Spin Master leading the charge as the property’s global master toy licensee. The firm will develop a range of pre-school toys based on the series. On top of this, Big Picture Licensing has signed up Penguin Random House as a strategic multi-territory licensee, joining Planeta Libra as publishing partners.

Brave Bunnies has already gone live in some territories, with further international roll-out scheduled for Q1 2021. A complimentary and comprehensive digital content plan is also in development. At MIPCOM last month, Brave Bunnies was the second most viewed show in the MIP Junior Screenings Library (and number one in its preschool target-demo), and unsurprisingly interest is brewing in the licensing arena.

Sergey Molchanov, CEO at Glowberry, said: “We have taken a lot of care to ensure that Brave Bunnies has received the best quality treatment from the off, and we are delighted to maintain that standard across our key commercial partner appointments.

“We’re grateful for the support and the broad positive response to our property, and we’re just getting started.”

Dan Frugtniet, MD at Big Picture Licensing, added: “We’re extremely proud and excited to be working with Glowberry on this wonderful property, and delighted, but not at all surprised at the strong start – without exception, everybody who we have showed Brave Bunnies to has been overwhelmingly positive about it.

“As well as finalising APAC agency appointments, we’re now looking to secure UK licensing partners in all major product categories. Please get in touch to discuss how you can hop on the Brave Bunny Bus.”

Brave Bunnies is an animated entertaining and educational 2D series for preschool kids (52 episodes, 7 minutes each). The main idea of the series is to show kids the diversity of the world around them, teach them to accept various traits of others and successfully communicate even with those who are completely different. Using the example of Brave Bunnies and their friends, parents can explain how to interact with other kids in the kindergarten or at the playground. In each episode, Brave Bunnies meet friends and come up with a fun game to play together.
